It was collected only from the upper castes
It was applicable only on Muslim marriages

question: Who was the father of Malik Ahmed, who founded 'Ahmednagar' after the disintegration of the Bahmani Empire?

question: The rulers of Vijayanagara assumed the title 'Narapati' (lord of men), then which title did the rulers of Odisha assume?

question: The architecture of 'Lotus Mahal' of Vijayanagar is a confluence of which two styles?

question: Who were called 'Kudirai Chettis' during the Vijayanagara period?

Foreign traders were given trading rights.
Brave soldiers were given Amaram Grams.

question: That Sultan of Bahmani Empire who was called 'Aristotle of Deccan' because of his 'peaceful policy' and scholarship?
solution: During his reign, Mohammed Shah II opened the treasury to aid the famine victims. The people liked him very much because of his generosity.

To show his aspiration to become a world conqueror
Because of his love for Greek culture

question: In which language is the book 'Amuktmalyada' written by Krishna Dev Rai written?

question: What was the function of 'Wazir-e-Ashraf' in the Bahmani Empire?

Villages whose revenue went directly to the royal treasury

question: Which ruler of Vijayanagara had entered into a treaty with the Portuguese Governor Albuquerque to monopolize the 'supply of horses'?

question: 'Kamalapuram Tank' was constructed by which ruler of Vijayanagara to meet the water requirements of the city?

question: Who was the Sultan of Delhi at the time of the establishment of Vijayanagara Empire?

It was the job of the priest only to perform the aarti of the temple.
Revenue collection and administration at the local level

question: Why did Bahmani Sultan Tajuddin Firoz Shah establish the city of 'Firozabad' (on the banks of river Bhima)?
options: As an alternative to his capital Gulbarga and a place of rest, Firoz Shah built this city with great grandeur as per his choice.
solution: Firozabad was famous for its architecture and beautiful gardens. Firoz Shah loved spending time here in pursuit of his multicultural interests.

question: What was the land given to the heroes of the 'Nayanakara system' in return for their services called during the Vijayanagara period?
solution: The main duty of the Amar-nayakas was to keep a certain number of soldiers and elephants ready for the king. They collected taxes from their area and sent a part of it to the king.

question: What was 'Kalyana Mandapam' in Vijayanagara Empire?

Special mandapas for wedding celebrations of deities in temples

question: Which dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire ruled for the shortest period (1485-1505)?

question: Which ruler of the Bahmani Empire bore the title of 'Amir-ul-Momineen' on his currency?

question: In which temple of Vijayanagara, Lord Vishnu is worshiped in the form of 'Vitthal'?

question: After the fall of the Bahmani Empire, which language was given royal patronage by the 'Adil Shahi' dynasty?

question: Who were the 'Nayakas' in the Vijayanagara Empire?

question: Which Sultan of Bahmani Empire gave literary patronage to 'Deccani' (Urdu-Hindi mixture) language?
solution: The Deccan language was a unique fusion of the Khari dialect of the North and the local languages ​​of the South. This language later laid the basis for the development of modern Urdu.

question: Which dynasty was established in 'Bijapur' after the fall of the Bahmani Empire?
solution: The Bahmani Empire broke up into five independent sultanates in the late 15th century. Bijapur was the most powerful among them. The 'Gol Gumbaz' here is an excellent example of architecture.

question: After which famous battle did the Vijayanagara Empire fall?
solution: In the battle of Talikota, the Sultans of Bijapur, Ahmednagar, Golconda and Bidar formed an alliance. The Vijayanagara army was led by Rama Raya, who was captured and killed during the battle.

question: Which was the first capital of the Bahmani Empire?
solution: The Bahmani Empire was the first independent Muslim state in South India. Many grand Bahmani mosques and mausoleums are still located in Gulbarga. Later the capital was moved to Bidar due to security reasons.

question: Which ruler of Vijayanagara recruited 'Turkish Archers' in the army to increase his military power?
solution: Deva Rai I gave complete freedom to the Muslim soldiers to practice their religion and also built a mosque for them in the city. This reflects his religious liberalism and practical military thinking.

question: During the reign of which ruler of Vijayanagara the famous Persian traveler 'Abdur Razzaq' came?
solution: Deva Raya II (1425-1446 AD) was the most glorious ruler of the Sangam dynasty. Abdur Razzaq has described seven levels of fortification of his city and described Vijayanagara as one of the most magnificent cities in the world.

question: Which is the site of Vijayanagara Empire which was declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 1986?
solution: Hampi is situated on the banks of Tungabhadra river. Virupaksha Temple, Vitthal Temple and Mahanavami Dibba are the most important attractions here. Colin Mackenzie discovered these ruins in 1800 AD.

question: Of which material is the foundation of 'Mahanavami Dibba' located in the royal center of Vijayanagara made?
solution: The carvings done on the outer walls of Mahanavami Dibba are still visible. This shows how amazing the artisans of Vijayanagara had a command over even a hard stone like granite.

question: 'Gol Gumbaz', situated in Bijapur, is whose tomb?
solution: Gol Gumbaz is a wonderful example of the Deccan style of architecture. Its 'Whispering Gallery' is so famous that even a slight noise made there echoes seven times.

question: Which Sultan of Bahmani Empire built 'Chand Minar' (not in Bidar, but in Daulatabad)?
solution: Chand Minar is considered to be the second tallest minar in India after Qutub Minar. It reflects the architectural excellence of the Bahmani Empire.

question: The post of 'Wazir-e-Ashraf' was related to which department in the Bahmani Empire?

question: Whose images have been found on 'Varaha' coins during the Vijayanagara period?

solution: The coins of Vijayanagara reflect their religious tolerance and respect for various Hindu sects (Shaiva and Vaishnava).

question: Which Wazir of the Bahmani Empire built a famous 'Madrasa' in Bidar?
solution: Mahmud Gawan's madrasa was three-storeyed and thousands of manuscripts were kept in it. Its architecture shows Persian influence.

question: What was the main objective of 'Zakat' tax in the Bahmani Empire?
options: There were other taxes to meet the expenses of the war.
The tax imposed on non-Muslims was called 'Jizya'.
Assistance to poor Muslims and religious work
The tax imposed on trade was called customs or custom duty.

question: Bahmani Sultan Firoz Shah Bahmani married the daughter of which ruler of Vijayanagara?
solution: Firoz Shah Bahmani was a learned Sultan who had great interest in science and literature. However, during his time there were continuous wars with Vijayanagara.

question: How are the roofs of the 'Elephant Stable' located in the royal center of Vijayanagara?
solution: The elephant stable was a symbol of the military power of Vijayanagara, where the state elephants were kept with royal pomp and show.

question: By whom was the 'Gopuram' (entrance) located in the 'Virupaksha Temple' of Vijayanagara mainly constructed?
solution: Gopuram is a distinctive feature of Vijayanagara architecture. These were so high that they indicated the presence of the temple from a distance. The Gopuram built by Krishna Deva Raya is also called 'Raya Gopuram'.

question: Which important territory did Krishna Deva Raya recover in 1520 by defeating Sultan Ismail Adil Shah of Bijapur?
solution: The Battle of Raichur (1520 AD) was one of the great military successes of Krishna Deva Raya. This victory made Vijayanagara the undisputed power of South India.

question: Which dynasty established its power in 'Bidar' after the fall of the Bahmani Empire?
solution: Bidar was the center of the Bahmani Empire, so here the last Sultans of the Bahmani dynasty ruled nominally for a long time, while the real power rested with the Burid Shahi ministers.

question: Which god was usually depicted on 'Varaha', the official currency of the Vijayanagara Empire?
solution: The coins of Vijayanagara were made of gold, silver and copper. The purity and weight of these coins reflect their prosperous trade relations.

question: Of the five states formed by the disintegration of the Bahmani Empire, which one was famous for 'diamond mines'?
solution: The trade of Golconda diamonds extended to Europe and Arabia. Historic diamonds like Kohinoor and Hope Diamond were obtained from this Sultanate.

question: In whose memory was the suburb named 'Nagalapuram' established by Krishna Deva Raya?
options: In memory of his father Tuluva Narasa Nayak
solution: Nagalapuram is located in today's Andhra Pradesh. The construction of new cities and temples by the Vijayanagara kings was a part of their luxurious lifestyle and public welfare.

question: In the administrative system of Vijayanagara Empire, 'Aygar system' was related to?
solution: The Aygar system was a unique system of rural self-governance. These 12 officials were given tax-free land in return for their services. Their posts were hereditary.

question: Which Sultan of the Bahmani Empire built inns and hospitals throughout the kingdom for the 'development of education'?
solution: The reign of Mohammad Shah II is considered a peaceful era of the Bahmani Empire. He also made arrangements for education for orphan children.

question: What was the meaning of the word 'Amaram' in the Vijayanagara period?
solution: The Amar-Nayak system was the backbone of Vijayanagara. These heroes gave annual gifts to the king and were present with their military contingents to assist the king during times of war. The Nayaks collected revenue from these areas.

question: 'Raichur Doab' was the fertile area between which two rivers during the Vijayanagara period?
solution: Raichur Doab was also called the 'granary of South India'. Whoever controlled this region ruled South India economically. Krishna Deva Raya finally won it for Vijayanagara in 1520.

question: The Bahmani Empire was divided into four administrative provinces, which were called?

question: Which Sultan of the Bahmani Empire invited 'foreign Muslims' (Afaqis) to settle in the Deccan?
solution: This policy of Ahmed Shah Wali gave capable officers to the Bahmani Empire, but it started a conflict between 'Afki' and 'Deccani' which led to the end of the empire.

question: Which style of architecture is influenced by the 'Prasaran Gallery' or 'Elephant Stables' of Vijayanagara?
solution: The Elephant Stable is located near the royal center of Hampi. It has 11 huge rooms, in which the royal elephants were kept. This shows the vastness of the military resources of Vijayanagara.

question: What did the Nayaks give to the king every year under the 'Nayankara system' during the Vijayanagara period?
options: A share of the revenue and gifts
solution: The main responsibility of the Nayakas was to provide military support to the king. However, the king could also transfer the Nayakas so as to control their power.

question: Which ruler of Vijayanagara used 'Portuguese guns and technology' to modernize his army?
solution: There were good relations between Krishna Deva Raya and the Portuguese Governor of Albuquerque. Portuguese gunners had greatly benefited Vijayanagara in its wars against Bijapur.

question: For what purpose were 'Kalyana Mandapa' temples used during the Vijayanagara period?
options: There were separate granaries for storing grains.
solution: The Kalyana Mandapa became an essential feature of Vijayanagara architecture. Fine carvings and beautiful sculptures were made on their pillars.

question: What was the meaning of the word 'Amaram' under the 'Nayanakara System' (Amara-Nayaka System) in the Vijayanagara period?
solution: The Amar-Nayaka system was a major political feature of Vijayanagara. These Nayaks provided military support to the king in times of need and collected revenue from their lands.

question: Where among the five successor states formed after the disintegration of the Bahmani Empire did the 'Adil Shahi' dynasty rule?
solution: The Bahmani Empire broke up into five independent sultanates in the late 15th and early 16th centuries: Bijapur (Adil Shahi), Ahmednagar (Nizam Shahi), Berar (Imad Shahi), Golconda (Qutb Shahi) and Bidar (Barid Shahi).

question: Which title was held by Harihara I, the founder of the Sangam dynasty?
solution: Harihara I (1336-1356 AD) was the first ruler of the Sangam dynasty. He played an important role in the early expansion of the empire and organized the administration.

question: Nicolo de Conti, who came during the Vijayanagara period, was a resident of which country?
solution: Niccolo de Conti has given a vivid description of the festivals of Vijayanagara, such as Diwali and Navaratri. He has told that the circumference of Vijayanagara was 60 miles.

question: Which Prime Minister of the Bahmani Empire increased the number of provinces (provinces) from 4 to 8?
solution: Mahmud Gawan was a very efficient administrator. He also reformed the revenue system and tried to control corruption.

question: Whom did the Sultanate of 'Bidar' help in the battle of Talikota after the fall of the Bahmani Empire?
options: The Barid Shahi Sultanate of Bidar was part of the confederacy formed against Vijayanagara, a confederacy of Muslim Sultans of the Deccan, which defeated Vijayanagara.
The Portuguese were seen as a neutral power.
There was always enmity between Bidar and Vijayanagara Empire.
solution: Although Bidar was a small sultanate, its contribution in the battle of Talikota was significant. It was only after the battle of Talikota that the independent power of Bidar gradually began to decline.

question: What does the carving of the 'Mahanavami Dibba' located in the royal center of Vijayanagara represent?
options: Scenes of hunting, war and festivals
Only the life of the common people
solution: The carvings on the Mahanavami box even today give us information about the military parade and folk culture of that time.

question: Whose local goddess was 'Pampadevi' during the Vijayanagara period?
options: Of the people living on the banks of the Tungabhadra River, Pampadevi is considered to be the human form of the Tungabhadra (Pampa) River.
There were separate totems only for traders.
solution: Hampi is named after Pampadevi and her marriage festival with Virupaksha is celebrated with great pomp even today.

question: Which great ruler of Vijayanagara composed the book named 'Amuktamalyada'?

question: Who built 'Gol Gumbaz' in 'Bijapur' after the fall of Bahmani Empire?
solution: Gol Gumbaz is famous for its 'Whispering Gallery', where even the slightest sound echoes several times.

question: In which temple of Vijayanagara, Lord Vishnu was worshiped in the form of 'Vitthal' and the famous 'Stone Chariot' is situated there?
solution: The construction of Vitthal Swamy temple started during the time of Deva Raya II and was further expanded during the time of Krishna Deva Raya. The stone chariot motif of the temple currently appears on the Indian ₹50 note.

question: What is the correct chronological order of the four important dynasties that ruled the Vijayanagara Empire?
solution: The history of Vijayanagara is divided into these four dynasties. The Sangam dynasty was founded by Harihara and Bukka, while the empire declined during the Aravidu dynasty and the capital was shifted to Penukonda.

question: Who among the 'Ashtadiggajas' is known as the 'Father of Telugu Poetry'?
solution: Krishna Dev Rai's court had become a center of literature and art because of the Ashtadigas. Allasani Pedanna was greatly respected by the king himself.

question: In which year was the 'Battle of Talikota', which ended the Vijayanagara Empire, fought?
solution: The battle of Talikota is also called the battle of 'Rakshasi-Tangadi'. In this Vijayanagara was defeated and the capital Hampi was completely destroyed. The army of Vijayanagara was led by Ram Rai.

question: Which ruler of Vijayanagara constructed 'Kamalapuram Reservoir' and 'Hiriya Canal' in his capital?
solution: The Vijayanagara Empire was known for its irrigation system. The Hiriya Canal still supplies water to parts of Hampi.

question: Which ruler of the Bahmani Empire received the patronage of 'Sufi saint Khwaja Banda Nawaz Gesuraja'?
solution: Gesudaraja was one of the most revered Sufi saints of the Deccan. His Dargah in Gulbarga is still a major center of communal harmony.

question: During the reign of which ruler, the construction of 'Vitthal Swami Temple' of Vijayanagara was completed and reached its peak grandeur?
solution: Vitthal Temple is the pinnacle of Vijayanagara architecture. Its 56 musical pillars and stone chariot attract tourists from all over the world. This is a symbol of the deep devotion of the Tuluva dynasty towards Lord Vishnu.

question: What is the correct descending order (from largest to smallest) of the administrative units of the Vijayanagara Empire?
solution: The administration of Vijayanagara was very well organized. The governors of the provinces were called 'Mandaleshwar'. There was a council of ministers to assist the king, which was headed by the 'Mahapradhan'.

question: What was the administrative system of Vijayanagara Empire related to 'Ayagar System'?
solution: The posts of 12 officials of the Aigar system were hereditary and they were given tax-free land in return for their services. This system strengthened rural self-governance.

question: What was the position of village officials in the 'Ayghar system' of Vijayanagara?
options: It was a permanent arrangement for only 5 years.
solution: The Aigar system was a strong pillar of rural self-governance, which provided stability to Vijayanagara for years.

question: How many musical pillars are there in 'Vitthal Swamy Temple' of Vijayanagar?
solution: The engineering of these pillars is still a subject of research for scientists as to how such sound can be extracted from stone.

question: Bahmani Sultan Tajuddin Firoz Shah defeated which ruler of Vijayanagara and married his daughter?
solution: The reign of Deva Raya I (1406–1422 AD) is known for constant conflict with the Bahmani Empire. Although they were initially defeated, they also successfully defeated Firoz Shah Bahmani in subsequent battles.

question: Who was the ruler among the Deccan Sultanates who wrote a book of music named 'Kitab-e-Nauras' and established the city of 'Nauraspur'?
solution: Due to the generosity of Ibrahim Adil Shah II, he was called the 'protector of the poor' (Abla Baba). His book 'Kitab-e-Nauras' is written in Deccani language and is based on musical ragas.

question: Which Wazir or Prime Minister of the Bahmani Empire built a famous three-storeyed Madrasa in Bidar?
solution: The Madrasa of Mahmud Gawan was a major center of Islamic education in medieval India. It contained thousands of books and scholars from all over the world came to study here. Mahmud Gawan also made revolutionary reforms in the Bahmani administration.

question: What was the post of 'Vakil-us-Sultanate' equivalent to in the Bahmani Empire?
solution: The division of posts in the Bahmani administration was very clear. While holding this post, Mahmud Gawan took the empire to its heights.

question: The post of 'Amir-e-Jumla' in the Bahmani Empire was related to?
solution: Amir-e-Jumla was a very important pillar of the Bahmani administration. The economic stability of the state depended on the efficiency of this officer.

question: Who wrote about the fortifications of the Vijayanagara Empire that "the city was surrounded by seven walls (tiers of fortifications)"?
solution: According to Abdur Razzaq, these walls surrounded not only the city but also agricultural fields and forests, to ensure food supply during the siege.

question: What was the word 'Pagoda' used for during the Vijayanagara period?
options: For the pinnacle of a temple
solution: There was an idol of the Varaha incarnation of Lord Vishnu on the Varaha coin, seeing which the foreigners named it Pagoda in their language. It was one of the most reliable currencies of the medieval period.

question: Bahmani Sultan Firoz Shah Bahmani defeated which ruler of Vijayanagara and received the area of ​​Bankapur as 'dowry'?
solution: The area of ​​Bankapur was fertile and strategically important. This treaty was humiliating for Vijayanagara, which was retaliated by subsequent rulers with military force.

question: In which part of Vijayanagar was 'Mahanavami Dibba' located and what was its use?
solution: The height of the Mahanavami Dibba was 40 feet and it was spread over 11,000 square feet. It has beautiful carvings on its walls, which depict scenes of hunting, war and dance.

question: Which Sultan of Bahmani Empire is known as 'Zalim' Sultan?
solution: Humayun Shah was the 11th Sultan of the Bahmani dynasty. During his reign, rebellions were suppressed with utmost cruelty, earning him this infamous title.

question: Which is the famous temple of Vijayanagara in whose premises the 'Stone Chariot' is located?
solution: The stone chariot is a unique example of the sculpture of Vijayanagara. It is so beautiful and lifelike that it is currently featured on the ₹50 note. The wheels of the chariot were made to rotate on their axis.

question: What is the literal meaning of the word Vijaynagar?
solution: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 on the banks of the Tungabhadra River. Its capital was Hampi, named after the local goddess Pampadevi. This empire is described in contemporary records as Karnataka Sampradayamu.

question: Which ruler of Vijayanagara established a suburb named 'Nagalapuram' in honor of his mother?
solution: Nagalapuram is located in present-day Chittoor district of Andhra Pradesh. The city reflects the tradition of respect that royal families had for their mothers and wives at that time.

question: Which ruler of the Bahmani Empire shifted his capital from Gulbarga to Bidar and named Bidar as 'Mohammadabad'?
solution: The geographical location of Bidar made it more capable of protecting itself from enemy attacks. Ahmed Shah Wali built many grand palaces and mosques here which are still a center of tourist attraction.

question: Which temple of Vijayanagara was called the 'Temple of Thousand Elephants' (not Vitthal Temple) - Hazara Ram Temple?
solution: Hazara Ram Temple is situated in the Royal Centre. Not only Ramayana but also beautiful processions of elephants and horses are depicted on its walls.

question: In which temple of Vijayanagar are beautiful carvings of 'ten incarnations of Vishnu' done?
solution: The temples of Vijayanagara were not only religious centers but also museums of art and culture. This carving done on stone is an example of the best sculpture of that period.

question: Which ruler of the Bahmani Empire built an observatory near Daulatabad to promote astronomy?
solution: Firoz Shah Bahmani had created a 'harem' for his wives which included women from different countries and he could speak to all of them in their mother tongue. He was one of the most educated Sultans of Deccan.

question: What is the meaning of 'Vijaynagar'?
solution: The Vijayanagara Empire is also described as 'Karnataka Empire' in contemporary records. It was founded by Harihara and Bukka.

question: 'Mustafi-e-Mamalik' was the head of which department in the Bahmani Empire?
solution: The Bahmani Sultans created a very organized administrative structure, which was inspired by the administrative model of the Delhi Sultanate. In this, after the Sultan, the position of Wazir or Vakil-of-the-Sultanate was the most important.

question: Where was the 'Observatory' built by Bahmani Sultan Tajuddin Firoz Shah located?
solution: Firoz Shah Bahmani is considered one of the most learned sultans of the Deccan. He knew many languages ​​and greatly promoted science and literature.

question: Which of the successor states of the Bahmani Empire was famous for its 'muslins and clothes'?
solution: Golconda clothes were in great demand among the royal houses of Europe. This trade made Golconda extremely prosperous economically.

question: Which Sultanate ultimately conquered 'Barar' among the successor states of the Bahmani Empire?
solution: There was also a fight for supremacy among the five Sultanates of Deccan. Berar was not involved in the battle of Talikota because it had a dispute with Ahmednagar.

question: After the fall of the Bahmani Empire, the area of ​​'Daulatabad' and 'Junnar' became the main center of which Sultanate?
solution: Ahmednagar's geographical location made it a buffer state between the Mughals and other Deccan states. The Nizam Shahi rulers here played a big role in preventing the Mughals from entering the Deccan.

question: Which ruler built the fort of 'Golkonda' after the fall of the Bahmani Empire? (initial form)
solution: Golconda was famous for its 'acoustics' and diamond mines. Kohinoor diamond was also discovered from here.

question: Which dynasty of the Vijayanagara Empire was founded by 'Tirumala' after the battle of Talikota?
solution: The Aravidu dynasty was the fourth and last dynasty of Vijayanagara. During this dynasty the power of the empire became very limited and it was limited to only some parts of the south.

question: What was the head of the 'Merchant Guilds' called during the Vijayanagara period?
solution: The foreign trade of the Vijayanagara Empire was extremely prosperous. Trade guilds had their own private armies and rules to protect trade.

question: What was 'Varaha' in Vijayanagara period?
options: The famous gold coin of Vijayanagara
solution: Varaha coins often bore figures of Hindu deities and animals (such as elephants or Garuda). Small gold coins were called 'Pratap' or 'Fanam'.

question: After the fall of the Bahmani Empire, which Sufi order had the most influence in 'Bijapur'?
solution: The famous Sufi saint Shah Aminuddin Ala of Bijapur wrote many religious texts in Deccani language. Sufism deeply influenced the social and cultural fabric of Bijapur.

question: Who was the Sultan of Bahmani Empire who changed the capital from Gulbarga to Bidar and was called 'Wali'?
solution: Ahmed Shah Wali built a grand fort and many tombs in Bidar. Bidar was chosen as the capital because of its climate and strategic location.

question: Who were the 'Nayakas' in the administrative system of Vijayanagara Empire?
options: Military commanders who were given territories to rule
The only civil officials who collected taxes
Priests who looked after the temple
solution: The 'Amar-Nayak' system of Vijayanagara was similar to the Iqta system of the Delhi Sultanate. These heroes provided military support to the king during times of war and also provided annual gifts.

question: What is the name of 'Ibrahim Rauza' built by the Sultanate of Bijapur after the fall of the Bahmani Empire?
solution: Ibrahim Rauza is famous for its intricate carvings and beautiful jaalis. It is considered to be one of the sources of inspiration for the construction of the Taj Mahal.

question: When the pillars of which temple of Vijayanagara are tapped, the sound of seven notes (Saregama) comes out?
solution: The Vitthala Swamy Temple is the culmination of Vijayanagara architecture. The stone chariot located in the temple complex is so finely carved that its wheels could actually rotate. It is dedicated to the Vitthal form of Lord Vishnu.

question: What was called 'Vipra' class in the social structure of Vijayanagara Empire?
solution: 'Agrahar' was donated by the state to Brahmins, which were tax-free. He was the chief patron of education and culture.

question: Which ruler of Vijayanagara married his daughter to the Bahmani Sultan Firoz Shah Bahmani?
solution: The reign of Deva Raya I (1406–1422 AD) is known for constant conflicts with the Bahmani Empire. He built a dam on the Tungabhadra River and constructed 'Hiriya Canal' for agriculture.

question: 'Kohinoor Diamond' was obtained from the mines of which famous Deccan Sultanate?
solution: Golconda was the global center of diamond trade in the medieval period. Marco Polo and the French traveler Tavernier have also praised the diamonds of Golconda.

question: Where is the tomb of Bahmani Sultan Ahmed Shah Wali located where Hindu-Muslim unity is celebrated even today?
solution: Ahmed Shah Wali is considered a saint because of his holiness. Hindu priests also perform rituals during their Urs (fair), which is symbolic of the Ganga-Jamuni culture of South India.

question: Which Sultan of Bahmani Empire is also known as 'Ahmad Shah Wali'?
solution: It was Ahmed Shah I who shifted the Bahmani capital from Gulbarga to Bidar. After his death his tomb in Bidar became a holy site where both Hindus and Muslims pay homage.

question: What was 'Nadu' during Vijayanagara period?
options: The king's bodyguard was called Garuda.
solution: Nadu was a very old and important unit of administration dating back to the Chola period. Vijayanagara further strengthened this system.

question: For what was the word 'Mahsul' used in the Bahmani Empire?
options: The customs duty imposed on foreign goods was called 'Zakat' or other trade tax.
The gift given to the Sultan was called 'Najrana'.
solution: Mahmud Gawan got the land measured for revenue collection and organized it to stop corruption. In the Bahmani Empire, 'Tarafdars' had a major role in revenue collection.

question: How many villages were generally included in the administrative unit called 'Sthala' during the Vijayanagara period?
solution: The administration of Vijayanagara was organized from bottom to top. The village administration was the responsibility of 'Aaygars', while the management of the site was looked after by officials like 'Amaldars'.

question: The traveler 'Abdur Razzaq' who came during the Vijayanagara period was the ambassador of which country?
solution: Abdur Razzaq has given a very impressive description of the fortifications and markets of Vijayanagara. He has written that there is no other city like Vijayanagar in the world.

question: Which Sultan of the Bahmani Empire started appointing Hindus in 'state functions'?
solution: The Bahmani Empire considered it necessary to take the support of the local population for its stability. This policy gave birth to a mixed culture (Deccani Culture) in Deccan.

question: Whose picture was usually printed on 'Varaha' coins during the Vijayanagara period?
options: Only the portrait of the king
These gold coins often bore the figures of Lord Venkateswara or the Varaha incarnation of Lord Vishnu.
solution: Varaha was the main basis of the currency system of Vijayanagara. This was a sign of the strength of business and economy.

question: Which is the platform located in the royal center of Vijayanagara which is 40 feet high and was used for royal rituals?
solution: Mahanavami Dibba was one of the highest and important sites of Vijayanagara. The social life of that time, dance, music and hunting scenes are depicted through carvings on its walls. This platform was a symbol of the grandeur and power of the king.

question: When was 'Hampi', the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO?
solution: Hundreds of temples, palaces and military structures of the Vijayanagara Empire exist in ruins in Hampi. It is considered to be the world's largest open-air museum.

question: What type of building was the 'Lotus Mahal' located in the royal center of Vijayanagara?
options: A council chamber where the king met with advisors
solution: The architecture of Lotus Mahal is an excellent example of Indo-Islamic style. A very beautiful coordination of arches and elements of Hindu architecture can be seen in it.

question: Which dynasty established its power in 'Bidar' after the fall of the Bahmani Empire?
solution: Bidar Sultanate was the smallest of the Deccan sultanates. In 1619 AD, it was annexed by the Adil Shahi Empire of Bijapur.

question: Which was the next largest unit after 'Gram' among the administrative units of Vijayanagara Empire?
solution: The administration of Vijayanagara was very organized. Village -> place -> nadu -> mandalam -> state. This well-organized structure kept the empire together for about 230 years.

question: To whom was the post of 'Sadr-us-Jahan' related to in the Bahmani Empire?
solution: The religious department in the Bahmani administration had a great influence on the society, especially in the matter of giving donations to saints.

question: Which ruler of Vijayanagara faced the combined Muslim confederacy in the battle of 'Rakshasi-Tangadi' (Talikota)?
solution: The battle of Talikota took place on 23 January 1565. Ram Rai was captured during the battle and beheaded by the Sultan of Bijapur. This war turned the glorious capital of Vijayanagara, Hampi, into ruins.

question: Which ruler of the Bahmani Empire, due to his cruelty, got his brother's 17 sons killed?
solution: These actions of Humayun Shah had created dissatisfaction within the Bahmani royal family. This is the reason why he has been stigmatized in history as 'tyrant'.

question: Where did the 'Nayaka' states emerge after the fall of the Vijayanagara Empire?
solution: The Nayaks of Madurai expanded the 'Meenakshi Temple', which is a testament to carrying forward the tradition of Vijayanagara architecture.

question: What was the shape of 'Gopuram' during Vijayanagara period?
solution: Gopurams were seen as symbols of power and devotion of the kings. 'Raya Gopuram' built by Krishna Deva Raya still stands proudly in the sky of Hampi.

question: Which ruler of Vijayanagara assumed the title of 'Gajabetekara' (hunter of elephants)?
solution: The power of Vijayanagara was reaching its peak during the time of Deva Raya II and he also strengthened the navy.

question: Which was the last dynasty of Vijayanagara Empire?
solution: The power of Vijayanagara gradually declined during the Aravidu dynasty. The last ruler of this dynasty was Sriranga III. The capital of the empire kept shifting from Hampi to Penukonda and then to Chandragiri.

question: For whom was the word 'Tarafdar' used in the Bahmani Empire?
solution: Tarfdars were very powerful in their area. They collected revenue and also maintained their own army, which sometimes made them a threat to the central authority.

question: By what title were the rulers of Vijayanagara known?
solution: The kings of Vijayanagara assumed grand titles to reflect their power and prestige. He also called himself 'Hindu Suratran' (protector of Hindu Sultans).

question: Where was the capital shifted after the fall of Vijayanagara Empire?
solution: After Penukonda the capital was also moved to Chandragiri, from where the last kings of Vijayanagara ruled.

question: Who was the Sultan of Bahmani Empire who is compared to 'Nero' because of his cruelty?
solution: During the reign of Humayun Shah, there were many rebellions which he suppressed with utmost brutality.

question: Which warfare method was adopted by 'Malik Ambar' in 'Ahmednagar' after the fall of Bahmani Empire?
solution: This method of Malik Ambar was later adopted by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and achieved success against the Mughals.

question: Who was the actual leader of the Vijayanagara army at the time of the Battle of Talikota (1565)?
solution: The Battle of Talikota was the beginning of the end for the Vijayanagara Empire. Due to the diplomatic failures of Rama Raya, the Sultans of Deccan formed a confederacy and badly defeated Vijayanagara and destroyed Hampi.

question: Which ruler of the Bahmani Empire built 'Jami Masjid' in the capital Gulbarga?
options: Firoz Shah Bahmani (or Mohammed Shah I)
solution: This mosque is said to be inspired by the style of the Cordova Mosque of Spain and is an early gem of Deccani architecture.

question: Which Prime Minister of the Bahmani Empire increased the number of provinces from 4 to 8 so that the power of the governors could be controlled?
solution: These reforms of Mahmud Gawan were not liked by the Tarafdars (governors), because it was reducing their autonomy. Due to this resentment, he listened to the Sultan and ultimately Mahmud Gawan got the death penalty.

question: Which Sultan of the Bahmani Empire shifted the capital from Gulbarga to Bidar?
solution: Bidar was considered superior to Gulbarga due to its climate and strategic location. Ahmad Shah Wali is also remembered for his close relationship with the Sufi saint Gesudaraja.

question: Which region was the major center of conflict between the Vijayanagara and Bahmani empires?
solution: Raichur Doab remained a 'bone of contention' due to its fertility and strategic location. Whoever controlled it influenced the politics of South India.

question: What is the interesting fact about the wheels of 'stone chariot' during Vijayanagara period?
options: They could actually rotate on their axis
They were just carvings, couldn't rotate
They were added much later by the British
solution: This chariot is the pinnacle of temple architecture. This shows that the artisans of Vijayanagara not only knew how to carve stone, but also had deep knowledge of engineering.

question: Which dynasty established power over Vijayanagara after the Sangam dynasty?
solution: The reign of the Saluv dynasty was short (1485-1505 AD). This dynasty is mainly known for saving the declining prestige of the empire and suppressing internal rebellions.

question: What was the post of 'Vakil-us-Sultanate' equivalent to in the Bahmani Empire?
solution: Mahmud Gawan has been the most famous lawyer-in-the-sultanate in the history of the Bahmani Empire, who strengthened the state.

question: Which fact is incorrect about the 'Mahanavami Dibba' located in the royal center of Vijayanagara?
options: There were carvings on its walls
It was spread over 11,000 square feet
It was merely a way into the temples
solution: Mahanavami Dibba was the center of power and celebrations of the king, where even foreign ambassadors were invited.

question: Which foreign traveler has described the practice of 'Sati' during the Vijayanagara period?
solution: The status of women was better in the society of Vijayanagara, but evils like the practice of Sati were also prevalent in some sections.

question: Which ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire was given the title of 'Gaja Betekara' (Hunter of Elephants)?
solution: Deva Raya II was the most powerful king of the Sangam dynasty. He also collected taxes from the kings of Sri Lanka and strengthened the navy of Vijayanagara.

question: Who was 'Gauda' in Vijayanagara Empire?
options: The chief tax collector was known as Tarafdar or by other names.
solution: The Gowda was assisted by 12 Aygars, from whom the administration of the village was run independently.

question: After the fall of the Bahmani Empire, which neighboring state was finally annexed by the Sultanate of Bijapur?
solution: Mutual conflict between the Deccan sultanates became the main reason for their decline. Taking advantage of this weakness, Aurangzeb later merged all of them into the Mughal Empire.

question: What was the name of the port of Bahmani Empire which was famous for importing horses from Persia and Iraq?
solution: Mahmud Gawan had snatched these ports from Vijayanagara so that the Bahmani Empire could have a monopoly on the horse trade.

question: Who abolished 'Marriage Tax' in Vijayanagara Empire?
solution: Marriage tax was collected from both the bride and groom. Its removal was a proof of Krishna Dev Rai's generosity and popular governance.

question: Where is the world's second largest dome 'Gol Gumbaz' located and who built it?
solution: The architect of Gol Gumbaz was 'Yakut of Dabul'. It is one of the largest dome structures in the world standing without any external support. The characteristic of its sound echo makes it unique.

question: By what title was Bahmani Sultan Humayun Shah known because of his cruelty?
solution: Humayun Shah's reign was short, but the stories of his cruelty are famous in history. However, he was the first Sultan to recognize the merits of Mahmud Gawan.

question: What was the place of 'ganikas' (devadasi system) in the social life of the Vijayanagara Empire?
options: They were not allowed to enter the temples
She worked only as a maid
They enjoyed a respectable position in society and participated in state festivals.
solution: Foreign travelers have described in detail the jewelery and splendor of these women of Vijayanagara. Their display during the festival of Mahanavami was a symbol of royal dignity.

question: Who founded the 'Barid Shahi' dynasty among the successor states of the Bahmani Empire?
solution: The Barid Shahi dynasty was also called the 'Foxes of the Deccan' because they enjoyed power for a long time by keeping the Bahmani Sultans under their influence.

question: In the history of Bahmani Empire, during whose reign did the Russian traveler named 'Afanasy Nikitin' come?
options: Mohammad Shah III (time of Mahmud Gawan)
solution: Nikitin's description shows that the life of the rich in the Bahmani Empire was extremely luxurious, while the condition of the common people was quite ordinary. He also mentions horse trade and the markets of Bidar.

question: In whose court did the Persian ambassador 'Abdur Razzaq' come during the Vijayanagara period?
solution: Abdur Razzaq was stunned to see the grandeur of Vijayanagara. He wrote that "Eye has never seen anything like it and ear has never heard anything like the city of Vijayanagara."

question: Who was the Sultan of Delhi Sultanate at the time of establishment of Vijayanagara Empire?
solution: The weakening of Tughlaq power in South India resulted in the rise of independent empires such as Vijayanagara (1336) and Bahmani (1347). Harihara and Bukka were first converted to Islam, but later converted back to Hinduism.

question: After the fall of the Bahmani Empire, who finally annexed Bijapur and Golconda into the Mughal Empire?
solution: After the merger of these Deccan sultanates, the Mughals gained direct control over South India, but due to this their conflicts with the Marathas became more intense.

question: The famous 'Kohinoor Diamond' was obtained from which mine of Deccan?
solution: Golconda Fort was the center of Qutb Shahi rulers. The diamonds here were exported to Persia and Europe. Marco Polo has also mentioned the diamonds of Golconda.

question: The 'Queen's Bath' located in the royal center of Vijayanagara shows the influence of which architectural style?
solution: The queen's bathroom looks simple from outside but is extremely ornate from inside. There was a big reservoir in the middle where fountains were installed and fragrant water flowed.
